title: NS-FAQ-01: Institutional Positioning & Governance Firewall
question: Is Nigeria Stack a government agency portal, a payment processor, or a commercial API store?
userTask: Verify the institutional role and governance rules of nigeriastack.org before adopting its technical specifications.
supportedEvidence: Under the Institutional Positioning Charter, nigeriastack.org is an independent public-domain specification commons aligned with federal technology standards and national interoperability guidelines.
materialLimit: nigeriastack.org holds no regulatory powers, processes no financial payments or digital currency transactions, hosts no toll-charging software services, and does not serve as a private vendor storefront.
nextAction: Review the Governance Charter and Non-Impersonation Notice in /governance or read NS-RFC-001.

title: NS-FAQ-02: Base Registry Autonomy & Data Sovereignty
question: Do government agencies like NIMC, CAC, NIBSS, NRS, or State Land Registries have to hand over their databases to use Nigeria Stack?
userTask: Connect statutory government registries to Nigeria Stack using secure, outward-facing verification tools.
supportedEvidence: Statutory institutions established under federal or state laws retain 100% legal ownership and control over their official master databases.
materialLimit: Connecting systems are strictly forbidden from copying or creating central shadow databases of national identity, banking, corporate, tax, or property records; all checks run as instant yes/no verification answers backed by secure cryptographic proof.
nextAction: Examine standard registry integration guidelines in /governance and test verification rules in /conformance.

title: NS-FAQ-03: Judicial Admissibility & Electronic Evidence
question: How does a Digital Evidence Seal (SureEvidence) make electronic court orders, land searches, and council certificates valid in court under Section 84 of the Evidence Act?
userTask: Issue and verify tamper-proof digital official records that satisfy Nigerian court admissibility rules without requiring expensive software licenses.
supportedEvidence: Digital seals embed verifiable document signatures, issuing device hardware details, automated counters, and legal compliance attestations into standard high-resolution QR codes printed on official forms.
materialLimit: If any text or number in an issued document is altered after printing, offline QR scanning detects the change immediately and alerts court officers that the document was modified.
nextAction: Scan a sample verified digital certificate offline in /conformance or read the digital proof standard in /protocols/sure-evidence.

title: NS-FAQ-04: Subnational Fiscal Autonomy & Revenue Directness
question: How does Direct Treasury Settlement (SplitDirect) guarantee that court fees, state taxes, and 774 Local Government revenues go straight to official public accounts?
userTask: Set up public payment channels for court filings, property rates, and municipal market fees that deposit revenues 100% directly into government treasuries.
supportedEvidence: In accordance with Section 121(3) of the Constitution and Supreme Court ruling SC/CV/343/2024, direct settlement rules prohibit holding public revenue in private middleman accounts or state joint holding accounts.
materialLimit: Any transaction configured to route core revenue into a private vendor or intermediary account is automatically blocked before payment processing begins.
nextAction: Review municipal payment guidelines in /rfcs/NS-RFC-014 and check direct treasury compliance tests in /conformance.

title: NS-FAQ-05: Offline-First Edge Operations & Clock Drift Resilience
targetPersonaCluster: Cluster 1 (Rural Courts, PHCs, and LGA Officers)
question: How do local courts, primary health clinics, and local government offices keep working when the power or mobile network goes down?
userTask: Run a lightweight, offline-first registry web application across remote public offices without relying on continuous power or mobile internet.
supportedEvidence: The offline registry engine uses a tiny app download under 35 KB that stores records securely on the local device and synchronizes automatically whenever internet connection is restored.
materialLimit: If an unpowered device's internal clock falls out of sync by more than five minutes, new entries are marked for time review and cannot be permanently sealed until clock accuracy is restored.
nextAction: Learn about offline application features in /protocols/kioskbase-registries and test time-drift recovery in /conformance.

title: NS-FAQ-06: Municipal Extortion Prevention & Transit Permits
question: How does the 774 Local Government Stack stop roadside cash touting (agbero extortion), fake market tickets, and multiple taxation of commercial vehicles?
userTask: Issue and verify shop permits, market tickets, and inter-council vehicle transit passes using secure digital checks.
supportedEvidence: Official fees paid by simple feature-phone USSD codes (*347*LGA#) or mobile payment terminals deposit 100% into council treasury accounts and generate instant digital QR passes.
materialLimit: Commercial trucks, buses, and delivery tricycles holding a valid digital transit pass verify offline in under a second across participating councils, preventing illegal roadside cash collection and double charging.
nextAction: Explore market collection tools in /protocols/lga-governance-stack/lga-10-market-collect and check council records in /atlas/lga-774.

title: NS-FAQ-07: Civic Attestation Integrity & SLA Protection
question: How does Digital Indigene & Residency Attestation (IndigeneProof) end forged paper letters and weeks of waiting at local council headquarters?
userTask: Apply for or verify official local government indigene and residency certificates for job, military, police, or university applications.
supportedEvidence: Digital indigene processes link clear citizen consent to simple USSD endorsement by recognized ward leaders and secure digital signatures from local council officials.
materialLimit: Council offices must process applications within a 72-hour service limit at published official fee rates, ending arbitrary delays and fake paper letters.
nextAction: Review indigene attestation rules in /protocols/lga-governance-stack/lga-06-indigene-proof and consent templates in /rfcs/NS-RFC-006.

title: NS-FAQ-08: Universal Accessibility & Non-Exclusion Standards
question: Can a citizen without a smartphone, internet data plan, or biometric token be turned away from local council, health, or court services?
userTask: Access public services like grievance reporting, vital registrations, market ticketing, or local healthcare using basic phones or walk-in service desks.
supportedEvidence: The Non-Exclusion Guarantee mandates that every service remains accessible via simple USSD codes (*347*LGA#), SMS notifications in five local languages (English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, and Pidgin), and standard paper counter options.
materialLimit: No citizen, farmer, or trader can be refused a public service simply because they do not own a smartphone, data plan, or digital device.
nextAction: Read the non-exclusion rule in /governance and examine implementation guides in docs/playbooks/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: NS-FAQ-09: Data Privacy & Consent Lifecycle Management
question: How do citizens and small businesses control who sees their personal or financial records under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023?
userTask: Manage clear data sharing approvals, expiration limits, and instant permission cancellations for banking, tax, health, and legal services.
supportedEvidence: Under data privacy standards, every shared data permission carries a clear expiration time and explicit purpose; revoking access stops data sharing across connected systems within 60 seconds.
materialLimit: Any system request using an expired or cancelled consent token is blocked immediately at the boundary with an access-denied error and zero database queries.
nextAction: Test expired consent protections in /conformance or inspect privacy schemas in /rfcs/NS-RFC-006.

title: NS-FAQ-10: Network Fault-Tolerance & Financial Idempotency
question: How does Safe Transaction Retry (Confluence) stop customers from being debited twice when a bank transfer or filing times out?
userTask: Prevent duplicate payments and repeated submissions when mobile network or banking connections experience delays.
supportedEvidence: System transport rules attach unique operation references to every transaction, safely holding dropped connections in an unresolved state rather than marking them as instant failures.
materialLimit: While a transaction status remains pending or unresolved, creating a new reference or retrying through a second provider is locked to prevent double debits.
nextAction: Review network retry specifications in /rfcs/NS-RFC-003 and run connection recovery tests in /conformance.

title: NS-FAQ-11: Legal Ethics, Privacy, & Judicial Protection
question: Why does Nigeria Stack ban lawyer "win-rate" rankings and lock sensitive family and juvenile court files?
userTask: Access court records, legal appearances, and case summaries while complying with legal ethics and privacy laws.
supportedEvidence: Legal specifications enforce neutral case outcome descriptions, official lawyer bar numbers, and strict row-level database security under Nigerian Bar Association Rule 39 and privacy laws.
materialLimit: Comparative lawyer win rates and automated judge profiling are blocked automatically, while family, custody, and juvenile records are restricted from public search access.
nextAction: Examine legal privacy rules in /conformance and inspect court data standards in /rfcs/NS-RFC-013.

title: NS-FAQ-12: AI Agent Delegation & Autonomous Guardrails
question: How does GivePower keep AI assistants safe so they cannot move money or file official records without human approval?
userTask: Integrate automated AI tools and assistant workflows under secure delegation rules.
supportedEvidence: Delegation standards enforce read-only access by default for AI tools, require human approval for official actions or updates, and place micro-payments into temporary holding that returns funds if a service fails.
materialLimit: Any automated action attempting to update official records without human authorization is denied immediately, and failed service calls automatically refund reserved funds to the caller.
nextAction: Inspect AI delegation gateway guides in /protocols/givepower-agents and test safety guardrails in /conformance.

title: NS-FAQ-13: Empirical Ecosystem Mapping & Non-Fabrication
question: Why does the 32-Industry Directory highlight existing Nigerian tech platforms first, and why does the State & Local Government Atlas avoid subjective ranking scores?
userTask: Review accurate technology coverage maps across 32 Nigerian economic sectors, 36 States, the FCT, and 774 Local Government Areas.
supportedEvidence: Industry mapping highlights established domestic technology providers—including NIBSS, Paystack, Moniepoint, Remita, Shipbubble, Termii, Dojah, Helium Health, and AFEX—before identifying service gaps, while subnational maps list verified statuses like Live Digital Service, Active Pilot, Paper-Only Registry, or Not Yet Assessed.
materialLimit: Directory lists avoid assuming a technology is missing simply because it is domestic, and state reports never claim a region is fully digitized if rural or local offices still rely on paper.
nextAction: Explore sector data in /sectors and state mapping datasets in /atlas/states.

title: NS-FAQ-14: Open Commons Integrity & The Five Tests
question: How does Nigeria Stack meet the Five Public Safeguards of Open Digital Infrastructure (Freedom to Exit, Open Source Code, Verifiable Audit, Inclusive Governance, and Freedom to Replicate)?
userTask: Inspect, adapt, or self-host Nigeria Stack specifications and developer toolkits on state, local government, or private infrastructure.
supportedEvidence: All specifications and datasets are published under public domain licenses (CC0-1.0), developer toolkits use open licenses, registries publish daily verification logs, working groups manage standards transparently, and open keys allow independent hosting.
materialLimit: No state government, local council, or software provider ever needs central permission, paid API keys, or commercial licenses from nigeriastack.org to verify digital proofs or switch software vendors.
nextAction: Check the Five Safeguards scorecard in /governance and access open repositories at github.com/nigeriastack.

title: NS-FAQ-15: Land & Agricultural Encumbrance Verification
targetPersonaCluster: Cluster 4 (Land Buyers, Farmers, and LGA Planners)
question: How do Digital Land & Farm Boundary Checks (LandGuard & AgriTrust) stop double-allocation of customary land and fraudulent property sales?
userTask: Verify whether a town plot, rural farm boundary, or local customary land right is free of ongoing court disputes or conflicting claims.
supportedEvidence: Land and agricultural verification tools connect mapped farm and plot boundaries directly to state court dispute registries and local customary court case logs.
materialLimit: Before land registries, banks, or local councils issue title certificates, crop financing, or customary rights of occupancy, any boundary overlap with an active court case raises an automatic dispute flag.
nextAction: Review land and agricultural specifications in /rfcs and check litigation clearance templates in /protocols.
